review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Before returning any computed money value, check ledgerly/money.py for helpers like round_money, to_money, and ZERO. Python round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals; the team convention is half-up to the cent via round_money.

item.title: Read existing sibling functions for conventions
item.description: Existing functions in the same module reveal the expected patterns (rounding, coercion, zero handling) to mirror.
item.content: When adding a new function, inspect neighboring functions like line_total and invoice_total first. They showed the pattern of to_money(...) coercion, round_money(...) wrapping, and sum(..., ZERO) accumulation, which the accepted implementation reused.

item.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
item.content: Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (imported from ledgerly.money) if it is falsy, before dividing. This satisfies the 'invoice without lines has average zero' requirement without special-casing empty lists separately.
